children: Iraq is negotiating with US energy companies Chevron and ExxonMobil over the development of major oilfields and associated infrastructure, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi said.

Chevron is in discussions with the Oil Ministry over the West Qurna 2 oilfield following the withdrawal of Russia's Lukoil due to sanctions, as well as the development of four blocks in the Nasiriyah field, the minister told the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The ministry is also holding discussions with ExxonMobil under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) covering the Majnoon oilfield, export infrastructure and a seawater supply project designed to provide 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) to support reservoir pressure.

Khudair said Iraq's oil agreements continued to follow a service-contract model, with the contractual framework evolving from the arrangements used during the initial licensing rounds in 2010 towards profit-sharing mechanisms rather than production-sharing agreements.
He said US and European companies favoured the revised approach, which the ministry considered effective in accelerating project implementation and generating financial returns for Iraq.
Separately, the ministry has activated a contract with US oilfield services company Halliburton to develop the Nahr Bin Umar and Sindbad oilfields.
It also has an MoU with ConocoPhillips for the development of the Akkas gas field, where SLB is working on the first phase.
The ministry has also activated a contract with HKN Energy for the development of the Hamrin oilfield, the minister said.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
